components.note: 母 (mǔ, 'mother') serves as the phonetic base; the sound has since diverged from měi, so the connection is mostly historical today.
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.

example.hanzi: 每人都能领到一份礼物。
example.pinyin: Měi rén dōu néng lǐng dào yī fèn lǐwù.
example.english: Everyone can receive a gift.
example.fact: The human body sheds roughly 30,000 to 40,000 skin cells every minute. Over the course of a decade, a person effectively replaces their entire outer layer of skin many times over, and household dust is partly made up of these shed cells.

components.note: 缶 (a clay jar) — 缺 relates to something broken or missing, like a cracked vessel.
夬 (guài) reflects the character's historical phonetic root, though the modern reading quē has diverged.
灬 (fire) — 点 originally related to a small flame or dot of light, giving rise to the meaning 'dot' or 'point.'
占 (zhàn) gives a hint of the sound — 点 is pronounced diǎn, a connection that has drifted over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有自己的缺点。
example.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu zìjǐ de quēdiǎn.
example.english: Everyone has their own shortcomings.
example.fact: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge in Washington collapsed in 1940 just months after opening, brought down by a design flaw that let wind trigger violent aerodynamic oscillations — a shortcoming that reshaped how engineers test bridges in wind tunnels ever since.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — relates to 设's meaning 'to establish, set up,' something first proposed through words.
殳 (shū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shè.
宀 (roof) — represents a home or fixed dwelling.
疋 (a foot/person) — a person settling down under a roof gave 定 its meaning 'to decide, to fix, to settle.'

example.hanzi: 你可以在手机里设定闹钟。
example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zài shǒujī lǐ shèdìng nàozhōng.
example.english: You can set an alarm on your phone.
example.fact: In 1884, delegates at the International Meridian Conference set up the system of 24 time zones anchored to the meridian running through Greenwich, England, standardizing clocks worldwide for the first time in history.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 挽 describes pulling or drawing something back with the hand.
免 (miǎn) gives a sound distantly related to 挽's reading wǎn, having drifted apart over time.
回 depicts a spiral or winding shape — something that turns back on itself, giving rise to the meaning 'to return.'

example.hanzi: 他努力挽回失去的信任。
example.pinyin: Tā nǔlì wǎnhuí shīqù de xìnrèn.
example.english: He worked hard to win back the trust he had lost.
example.fact: NASA's Apollo 13 mission suffered an oxygen tank explosion in April 1970, roughly 200,000 miles from Earth, but flight controllers and the crew improvised fixes using onboard materials to bring all three astronauts home safely.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) shows 遥 relates to distance traveled.
䍃 gives a sound close to yáo, sharing the vowel sound.
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 远's meaning 'far, distant,' a long way to walk.
元 (yuán) gives a sound hint — 远 is pronounced yuǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 那颗星星距离我们非常遥远。
example.pinyin: Nà kē xīngxīng jùlí wǒmen fēicháng yáoyuǎn.
example.english: That star is extremely far from us.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is now more than 24 billion kilometers from Earth, making it the most distant human-made object in existence; its radio signals still take over 22 hours to reach us.

components.note: 止 (a foot), shown in an inverted form at the top of the character, represents forward motion.
舟 (a boat) originally sat below the foot; stepping into a boat to move onward gave 前 its meaning 'front, ahead, before.'
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'

example.hanzi: 许多游客前来参观故宫。
example.pinyin: Xǔduō yóukè qiánlái cānguān Gùgōng.
example.english: Many tourists come to visit the Forbidden City.
example.fact: Beijing's Forbidden City, completed in 1420, contains 980 surviving buildings and nearly 9,000 rooms, and served as the imperial palace for 24 emperors across the Ming and Qing dynasties.

components.note: 单 (in its traditional form 單) depicts an ancient forked hunting tool, resembling a sling or trap; the picture of this single tool was later borrowed to represent the idea of 'single, sole, only.'
讠 (speech) — 词 names a word, a unit of speech.
司 (sī) gives the sound — an exact match with 词.

example.hanzi: 这本词典收录了十万个单词。
example.pinyin: Zhè běn cídiǎn shōulù le shí wàn gè dāncí.
example.english: This dictionary contains 100,000 words.
example.fact: The Oxford English Dictionary contains entries for over 600,000 words, and compiling its first edition, published in 1928, took editors more than 70 years from the project's original start.

components.note: 王 (a variant of 玉, meaning jade) — 球 originally referred to a round piece of jade, extended to mean 'ball, sphere'
求 (qiú) gives the sound — 球 is also pronounced qiú, an exact match
辶 (to walk) — 迷 originally described losing one's way while walking, extending to 'confused, obsessed.'
米 (mǐ) gives a sound distantly related to mí, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 世界杯期间,球迷们彻夜狂欢。
example.pinyin: Shìjièbēi qījiān, qiúmímen chèyè kuánghuān.
example.english: During the World Cup, fans celebrate all night.
example.fact: The 2014 FIFA World Cup final in Brazil drew a global television audience estimated at over one billion viewers, making it one of the most-watched sporting events in human history.

components.note: 彡 (fine lines, streaks) — 彩 relates to patterns and bright colors.
采 (cǎi) gives the sound — an exact match with 彩's reading cǎi.
扌 (hand) — 排 relates to arranging things by hand into order
非 (fēi) gives a sound distantly related to 排's reading pái, having drifted apart over time

example.hanzi: 演员们正在为首演彩排。
example.pinyin: Yǎnyuánmen zhèngzài wèi shǒuyǎn cǎipái.
example.english: The actors are rehearsing for opening night.
example.fact: In January 1967, a flash fire broke out aboard Apollo 1 during a launch-pad rehearsal, killing all three astronauts and prompting NASA to redesign the capsule's hatch, materials, and safety procedures before any further crewed flights.

components.note: 隹 (a bird) — one of a flock.
木 (a tree) — birds flocking together on a tree, the image of gathering that gave 集 its meaning 'to gather, collect; a collection.'
亻 (a person) shows that 体 relates to the human body.
本 (běn) is close in sound to 体's reading tǐ, though the connection has drifted somewhat over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 学校组织了一次集体旅行。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào zǔzhī le yī cì jítǐ lǚxíng.
example.english: The school organized a group trip.
example.fact: Flocks of starlings can form massive, shifting shapes called murmurations, sometimes involving hundreds of thousands of birds that coordinate their movements within a fraction of a second of each other, with no leader directing the group.

meanings: to put one's hand to it
to start out on a task

components.note: 艹 (plants, grass) — 着 (a simplified variant of 著) originally related to placing or attaching things, a sense rooted in arranging plant material.
者 (zhě) is close in sound to 着's reading zhuó, sharing the same historical phonetic root as 著.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

example.hanzi: 政府已经着手解决交通问题。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ yǐjīng zhuóshǒu jiějué jiāotōng wèntí.
example.english: The government has begun to address the traffic problem.
example.fact: In 1956, the United States began construction of its Interstate Highway System under President Eisenhower, eventually building over 77,000 kilometers of roadway in what was then the largest public works project in the country's history.

components.note: 日 (sun) — 星 relates to bright heavenly bodies like the sun and stars
生 (shēng) gives a sound close to 星's reading xīng
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
三 is made of three simple horizontal strokes stacked together — the most direct way to picture the number three, following the same pattern as 一 (one) and 二 (two).

example.hanzi: 我们星期三有一场考试。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xīngqīsān yǒu yī chǎng kǎoshì.
example.english: We have an exam on Wednesday.
example.fact: The English name 'Wednesday' comes from 'Woden's day,' honoring the Germanic god Woden (Odin), while several Romance languages, such as Spanish 'miércoles,' instead preserve the older Roman name for Mercury's day.

components.note: 己 (a kneeling child) — the one being disciplined.
攵 (a hand with a stick) — correcting the child, giving 改 its meaning 'to change, correct, reform.'
辶 (to walk) — 进 relates to advancing or entering, both movement-related.
井 (jǐng) gives a close sound cue — 进 is pronounced jìn, sharing similar consonant and vowel sounds.

example.hanzi: 工程师不断改进产品的设计。
example.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī bùduàn gǎijìn chǎnpǐn de shèjì.
example.english: Engineers keep improving the product's design.
example.fact: Toyota's production system popularized 'kaizen,' a philosophy of continuous incremental improvement that empowers factory workers to halt the assembly line themselves the moment they spot a defect, rather than letting problems pile up downstream.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洋 refers to the vast ocean
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — an exact match with 洋's reading yáng
艹 (plant) — 葱 names a type of vegetable plant.
怱 (cōng) gives the sound — an exact match with 葱's reading.

example.hanzi: 妈妈在切洋葱的时候流眼泪了。
example.pinyin: Māma zài qiē yángcōng de shíhòu liú yǎnlèi le.
example.english: Mom cried while cutting onions.
example.fact: Cutting an onion ruptures its cells and triggers a chemical reaction that produces syn-propanethial-S-oxide, a volatile gas that drifts up and irritates the eyes, causing the classic reflexive tears.

components.note: 大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.
钅 (metal) — 衔 originally referred to a metal bit held in a horse's mouth.
行 (xíng) gives a sound close to xián, sharing the initial with a rhyme that has drifted over time.

example.hanzi: 他获得了博士头衔。
example.pinyin: Tā huòdé le bóshì tóuxián.
example.english: He earned the title of doctor.
example.fact: Guinness World Records lists the full ceremonial name of Bangkok as one of the longest place names in the world, running 169 letters, even though residents and official maps simply shorten it to Krung Thep.

components.note: 牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
亻 (a person) shows that 体 relates to the human body.
本 (běn) is close in sound to 体's reading tǐ, though the connection has drifted somewhat over the centuries.

example.hanzi: 那个物体从天上掉了下来。
example.pinyin: Nàge wùtǐ cóng tiān shàng diào le xiàlái.
example.english: That object fell from the sky.
example.fact: The Chelyabinsk meteor that exploded over Russia in 2013 released an estimated 500 kilotons of energy — roughly 30 times the force of the Hiroshima bomb — and injured over 1,000 people, mostly from shattered window glass.

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烧 describes burning or cooking with fire.
尧 (yáo) gives a rhyme close to shāo, with a different initial.
火 (fire) — 烤 describes cooking directly over fire or heat.
考 (kǎo) gives the sound — an exact match with 烤.

example.hanzi: 周末我们打算去海边烧烤。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen dǎsuàn qù hǎibiān shāokǎo.
example.english: This weekend we plan to have a barbecue at the beach.
example.fact: The English word 'barbecue' likely descends from 'barbacoa,' a term Spanish colonizers borrowed from the Taíno people of the Caribbean for a wooden framework used to slow-cook meat over an open fire.

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 途 names a road or path traveled on.
余 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tú, having drifted apart over time.
彳 (to walk, step) — 径 names a small path for walking.
工 (gōng) gives a sound distantly related to jìng, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我们需要找到解决问题的途径。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào zhǎodào jiějué wèntí de tújìng.
example.english: We need to find a way to solve the problem.
example.fact: The ancient Silk Road was never a single road but a sprawling network of trade routes stretching over 6,400 kilometers, connecting China to the Mediterranean and carrying silk, spices, and eventually diseases like the plague.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 激 originally described water dashing or surging forcefully
敫 (jiǎo) gives a sound distantly related to 激's reading jī, having drifted apart over time
儿 (a person) — shown carrying a torch overhead, the source of 光's meaning 'light, brightness.'
火 (fire) — the torch's flame, the thing giving off the light.

example.hanzi: 医生用激光治疗他的眼睛。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng yòng jīguāng zhìliáo tā de yǎnjīng.
example.english: The doctor used a laser to treat his eyes.
example.fact: The first working laser was built in 1960 by physicist Theodore Maiman at Hughes Research Laboratories using a ruby crystal; some skeptics at the time reportedly dismissed it as 'a solution looking for a problem.'

components.note: 犭 (animal) — 狐 names an animal, the fox.
瓜 (guā) gives a sound only distantly related to hú today, having drifted apart over time.
犭 (animal) — 狸 names a small mammal, grouped with other animal characters.
里 (lǐ) gives a sound close to lí, the same syllable with a different tone.

example.hanzi: 一只狐狸悄悄地溜进了鸡舍。
example.pinyin: Yī zhī húli qiāoqiāo de liūjìn le jīshè.
example.english: A fox quietly slipped into the henhouse.
example.fact: Red foxes can reportedly hear a watch ticking from about 40 meters away, and some researchers believe they use Earth's magnetic field to help judge distance when pouncing on prey hidden under snow.

meanings: a stumbling block on the path to enlightenment

components.note: 冖 (a roof/house) — the home being welcomed into.
友 (a friend) — brought close into one's home; the traditional form 愛 also includes 心 ('heart') in the middle — the source of 爱's meaning 'to love.'
氵 (water) — 河 relates to rivers and waterways
可 (kě) gives a sound close to 河's reading hé

example.hanzi: 情人节那天,很多情侣在爱河边散步。
example.pinyin: Qíngrénjié nà tiān, hěnduō qínglǚ zài Àihé biān sànbù.
example.english: On Valentine's Day, many couples stroll along the Love River.
example.fact: Kaohsiung's Love River in southern Taiwan was once so polluted by industrial waste that boats couldn't pass through it, but a major cleanup effort starting in the 1980s transformed it into a lit promenade now popular for evening river cruises.

components.note: 凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.

example.hanzi: 这两个双胞胎穿着同一件衣服。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè shuāngbāotāi chuānzhuó tóngyī jiàn yīfú.
example.english: These twin siblings are wearing identical clothes.
example.fact: Even genetically identical twins don't share fingerprints — the ridge patterns form from tiny, random differences in pressure and position inside the womb, so despite matching DNA, each twin's prints remain unique.

components.note: 户 (door) — 房 relates to a room or house, a space behind a door
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 房 is pronounced fáng, a close match
土 (earth/soil) — 地's original meaning is 'earth, ground'
也 (yě) gives a partial sound match for 地's other reading dì; in this grammatical-particle usage the character is instead pronounced 'de'
厂 (chǎng) gives a hint of the sound — 产 is pronounced chǎn, nearly identical apart from the final consonant.

example.hanzi: 房地产价格这几年涨了很多。
example.pinyin: Fángdìchǎn jiàgé zhè jǐ nián zhǎng le hěnduō.
example.english: Real estate prices have risen a lot in recent years.
example.fact: In 1626, the Dutch West India Company reportedly acquired Manhattan Island from local Lenape inhabitants for goods valued around 60 guilders — a story often retold, if imprecisely, as history's most lopsided real-estate deal.

components.note: 永 pictures a river branching and forking into smaller streams; water flowing on and on gave the character its meaning 'perpetual, forever.'
久 originally pictured a person's leg being restrained or held in place — something kept fixed for a long stretch of time — which gave the character its meaning 'long-lasting, prolonged.'

example.hanzi: 这份合同不是永久有效的。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn hétóng bùshì yǒngjiǔ yǒuxiào de.
example.english: This contract is not permanently valid.
example.fact: Some radioactive isotopes found in nuclear waste, such as iodine-129, have half-lives of about 15.7 million years, meaning the material stays hazardous for a span of time far longer than all of recorded human history.

components.note: 日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form
髟 (long hair) — 髦 (fashionable; a child's flowing hair) is rooted in hairstyle.
毛 (máo) gives the sound — an exact match with 髦's reading.

example.hanzi: 她总是穿得很时髦。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒng shì chuān de hěn shímáo.
example.english: She always dresses very fashionably.
example.fact: In the 1920s, 'flapper' fashion in the West dramatically shortened hemlines and popularized bobbed hair, a stylistic shift so sudden that some contemporary newspapers described it as evidence of moral decline.

components.note: Hand radical — choosing or picking out involves the hand.
Provides a reading close to but not identical to modern 'jué'; originally related to the idea of breaking off or separating something, echoing the act of picking one option out from others.
扌 (hand) shows that 择 relates to selecting or picking something out by hand.
睪 (yì) is close in sound to 择's reading zé, and appears as the shared phonetic element across a family of characters that includes 泽, 译, and 驿.

example.hanzi: 面对两份工作,他很难做出抉择。
example.pinyin: Miànduì liǎng fèn gōngzuò, tā hěn nán zuò chū juézé.
example.english: Faced with two job offers, he found it hard to make a choice.
example.fact: Psychologists studying 'choice overload' found that shoppers offered 24 varieties of jam at a tasting booth were far less likely to actually buy any than those offered just six, suggesting too many options can make deciding harder rather than easier.

components.note: 丑 originally depicted a hand with bent, claw-like fingers, and was used to write the second of the twelve Earthly Branches (traditionally paired with the ox in the Chinese zodiac). The glyph was later borrowed to also write the unrelated word for 'ugly,' since the two words sound alike.
耳 (ear) — 闻 originally meant 'to hear,' later extending to 'smell' and 'news.'
门 (mén) contributes the rhyme -en, close to wén's sound, though the initial has since shifted.

example.hanzi: 这起丑闻震惊了整个政界。
example.pinyin: Zhè qǐ chǒuwén zhènjīng le zhěnggè zhèngjiè.
example.english: This scandal shocked the entire political world.
example.fact: The Watergate scandal began with a botched burglary at the Democratic National Committee headquarters in 1972 and eventually led to President Richard Nixon's resignation in 1974, the only U.S. president ever to resign from office.

components.note: 又 (hand), doubled — two hands side by side depict a pair, giving 双 its meaning 'pair, both, two.'
千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'

example.hanzi: 他拥有双重国籍。
example.pinyin: Tā yōngyǒu shuāngchóng guójí.
example.english: He holds dual citizenship.
example.fact: The double-slit experiment shows that light, and even individual electrons, can behave as both particles and waves — a phenomenon called wave-particle duality that puzzled and fascinated physicists throughout the early 20th century.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 脚 refers to the foot, a part of the body
却 (què) gives a sound distantly related to 脚's reading jiǎo, having drifted apart over time
足 (foot) — the ankle is part of the foot and leg joint system.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound now quite distant from 踝's reading huái — the phonetic link has drifted significantly over time.

example.hanzi: 她打篮球的时候扭伤了脚踝。
example.pinyin: Tā dǎ lánqiú de shíhòu niǔshāng le jiǎohuái.
example.english: She twisted her ankle while playing basketball.
example.fact: Ankle sprains are among the most common sports injuries, accounting for an estimated two million cases a year in the United States alone, and most involve overstretching the ligaments on the outer side of the joint.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
钅 (metal/gold) — represents something valuable.
昔 (formerly, in the past) — valuable metal that has been mishandled or lost over time gave 错 its meaning 'mistake, wrong.'

example.hanzi: 程序在运行时出错了。
example.pinyin: Chéngxù zài yùnxíng shí chūcuò le.
example.english: The program encountered an error while running.
example.fact: NASA lost the $327 million Mars Climate Orbiter in 1999 because one engineering team used metric units while another used imperial units for a key navigation calculation, sending the spacecraft too close to Mars and destroying it.

components.note: 石 (stone) — 硬 describes something as hard and firm as stone.
更 (gèng) gives a sound distantly related to yìng, having drifted apart over time.
皿 (dish) — 盘 names a flat dish or tray.
般 (bān) gives a sound distantly related to pán, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 我的硬盘存储空间已经满了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de yìngpán cúnchú kōngjiān yǐjīng mǎn le.
example.english: My hard disk storage is already full.
example.fact: IBM introduced the first commercial hard disk drive in 1956, the RAMAC 350, which stored just 5 megabytes of data across fifty 24-inch platters and weighed over a ton — less storage than a single modern photo.

components.note: 五 places an X-shaped cross between two horizontal lines representing heaven and earth — in traditional cosmology, this was linked to the five elements that fill the space between.
十 is thought to derive from a knot tied in a cord — early counting systems used knotted ropes to keep tallies, and a single cross-stroke came to stand for the number ten.

example.hanzi: 这个班一共有五十个学生。
example.pinyin: Zhège bān yīgòng yǒu wǔshí gè xuéshēng.
example.english: This class has fifty students in total.
example.fact: A couple's fiftieth wedding anniversary is traditionally called the 'golden anniversary,' a custom said to date back to at least medieval Germany, where husbands crowned their wives with a wreath of gold on that milestone.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) gives a sound hint — 英 is pronounced yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
文 depicts a chest marked with crossing lines, once tattoos or patterns on the body — decoration and pattern gave rise to the idea of 'writing' and 'culture.'

example.hanzi: 他能说流利的英文。
example.pinyin: Tā néng shuō liúlì de Yīngwén.
example.english: He can speak fluent English.
example.fact: English has roughly 1.5 billion speakers worldwide when counting both native and second-language speakers — more than any other language — even though Mandarin has far more native speakers alone.

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
足 (foot) — relates to 路's meaning 'road, path,' something walked on with feet.
各 (gè) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from lù.

example.hanzi: 天还没亮,他们就上路了。
example.pinyin: Tiān hái méi liàng, tāmen jiù shàng lù le.
example.english: Before dawn, they had already set out on their journey.
example.fact: U.S. Route 66, established in 1926, stretched roughly 3,940 kilometers from Chicago to Santa Monica and became a symbol of the American road trip before being officially decommissioned in 1985 as interstate highways took over.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — relates to 照's meaning 'to shine, illuminate; photograph.'
昭 (zhāo) gives a sound hint — 照 is pronounced zhào, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'

example.hanzi: 游客们都在长城上照相。
example.pinyin: Yóukè men dōu zài Chángchéng shàng zhàoxiàng.
example.english: Tourists are all taking photos on the Great Wall.
example.fact: The earliest surviving photograph of a person was taken in 1838 by Louis Daguerre on a Paris boulevard; a man having his shoes shined stood still long enough during the multi-minute exposure to be captured, while everyone else on the busy street blurred into invisibility.

components.note: 力 (strength) — 加 pictures adding one's effort to a cause.
口 (mouth, words) — combining strength with words of support gave 加 its meaning 'to add' or 'to increase.'
氵 (water) — 油 names an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 油.
立 (to stand) — 站 relates to standing, and by extension a stop or station where one stands to wait
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 站 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match

example.hanzi: 车快没油了,我们得找个加油站。
example.pinyin: Chē kuài méi yóu le, wǒmen děi zhǎo gè jiāyóuzhàn.
example.english: The car is almost out of gas, we need to find a gas station.
example.fact: The world's first drive-in gas station opened in Pittsburgh in 1913, run by the Gulf Refining Company, which gave away free road maps to attract customers in the early days of automobile travel.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — the mouth radical, marking the character as related to speech, sound, or an action of the mouth.
劳 (láo) gives the sound — an exact match with 唠's reading.
口 (mouth) — 叨 relates to talking.
刀 (dāo) gives the sound — an exact match with 叨's reading.

example.hanzi: 妈妈总是唠叨我要早点睡觉。
example.pinyin: Māma zǒng shì láodao wǒ yào zǎodiǎn shuìjiào.
example.english: Mom always nags me to go to bed early.
example.fact: The phrase 'broken record,' often used to describe someone who repeats themselves annoyingly, comes from vinyl records that would skip on a physical scratch and replay the same short phrase over and over.

components.note: 高 depicts a tall tower or palace, with a roof at the top and a base below — a simple picture of height.
足 (foot) — 跟 originally referred to the heel of the foot, extended to mean 'to follow (on someone's heels)'
艮 (gèn) gives a loose sound connection to 跟's reading gēn
革 (leather) shows 鞋 is typically made of leather.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to xié, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 她穿着高跟鞋走了一整天,脚很疼。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhuó gāogēnxié zǒu le yī zhěngtiān, jiǎo hěn téng.
example.english: She walked all day in high heels, and her feet hurt a lot.
example.fact: High heels were originally worn by 10th-century Persian cavalry soldiers to help their feet stay locked in the stirrups; European aristocrats adopted the style in the 1600s as a fashionable status symbol long before it became associated mainly with women's wear.

components.note: 火 (fire) — the fire radical, marking the character as related to fire, heat, or burning.
玄 (xuán) gives a sound close to 炫's reading xuàn — the same syllable, differing only in tone.
Light — represents brightness.
A bird with long, shining feathers, like a peacock's tail.

example.hanzi: 他喜欢在朋友面前炫耀自己的新车。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuān zài péngyǒu miànqián xuànyào zìjǐ de xīn chē.
example.english: He likes to show off his new car in front of friends.
example.fact: A peacock's iridescent tail feathers can span over a meter and number more than 200; Darwin himself worried that such an elaborate, seemingly impractical display contradicted natural selection until he worked out how mate choice could favor it.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — relates to 技's meaning 'skill, technique,' a skill performed with the hands.
支 (zhī) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jì.
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 学一门新技能需要花很多时间。
example.pinyin: Xué yī mén xīn jìnéng xūyào huā hěnduō shíjiān.
example.english: Learning a new skill takes a lot of time.
example.fact: The famous claim that mastering a skill requires exactly 10,000 hours of practice originated from a popular misreading of psychologist Anders Ericsson's research on violinists; Ericsson himself said the real driver is the quality of deliberate practice, not a fixed number of hours.

components.note: 身 depicts a person's torso, originally showing a pregnant woman's body — later broadened to mean 'the body' in general.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.

example.hanzi: 天气冷了,要注意保护身子。
example.pinyin: Tiānqì lěng le, yào zhùyì bǎohù shēnzi.
example.english: The weather has turned cold, so take care to protect your body.
example.fact: An adult human skeleton has 206 bones, down from roughly 300 present at birth — many bones, especially in the skull, naturally fuse together as a child grows.

components.note: Hand — shows this is a physical action.
Represents fighting or striving for something.
钅 (metal) — 钱 relates to money, since early Chinese coins were made of metal
戋 (jiān) gives a loose sound connection to 钱's reading qián

example.hanzi: 他每天工作十个小时来挣钱养家。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān gōngzuò shí gè xiǎoshí lái zhèngqián yǎngjiā.
example.english: He works ten hours a day to earn money to support his family.
example.fact: The U.S. Bureau of Engraving and Printing produces around 38 million banknotes a day, worth roughly $560 million, using paper made from a cotton-linen blend rather than ordinary wood-pulp paper.

components.note: 屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
禾 (grain) — 租 originally described tribute paid in grain.
且 here marks the payment as regular and ongoing — combined with the grain 禾, it gave 租 its meaning 'rent, tax.'

example.hanzi: 他把多余的房间出租给了学生。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ duōyú de fángjiān chūzū gěi le xuésheng.
example.english: He rented out the spare room to a student.
example.fact: Ancient Rome had multi-story rental apartment buildings called insulae, some reportedly rising six or seven stories, and they housed the majority of the city's population who couldn't afford a private house of their own.

components.note: 臣 here represents a person bending forward, with an eye looking downward.
皿 (a basin holding water) served as an early mirror; a person peering down into the basin's reflection gave 监 its meaning 'to observe, supervise.'
见 (to see) — relates directly to 视's meaning 'to look at, view.'
礻 (a form of 示, shì) gives the sound — 视 is also pronounced shì, an exact match.
口 (a vessel), shown four times — a set of cooking vessels.
犬 (a dog) — guarding the vessels, the source of 器's meaning 'vessel, tool, instrument.'

example.hanzi: 银行大厅里安装了监视器。
example.pinyin: Yínháng dàtīng lǐ ānzhuāng le jiānshìqì.
example.english: Security cameras were installed in the bank's lobby.
example.fact: The first CCTV system was installed in 1942 by German engineer Walter Bruch to observe V-2 rocket launches remotely, decades before surveillance cameras became a routine fixture of city streets and shops.

components.note: 画 depicts a picture set within a frame — the traditional form 畫 additionally showed a hand holding a brush above it.
广 (a building, shelter) — a corridor is part of a building.
郎 (láng) gives the sound — an exact match for 廊.

example.hanzi: 这家画廊正在展出印象派的作品。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā huàláng zhèngzài zhǎnchū yìnxiàngpài de zuòpǐn.
example.english: This gallery is currently exhibiting Impressionist works.
example.fact: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most-visited art museum, drawing close to nine million visitors a year, and its glass pyramid entrance, added in 1989, was fiercely controversial at the time for clashing with the historic palace's classical facade.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 帕 names a small piece of woven cloth.
白 (white, plain) — a plain white cloth 巾 gave 帕 its meaning 'kerchief, scarf.'
牛 (ox) — 特 originally referred to a male ox singled out for sacrifice, a special animal set apart from the herd.
寺 (sì) gives a hint of the sound — 特 is pronounced tè, a connection that has drifted over time.
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'

example.hanzi: 我的同事帕特里克来自爱尔兰。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de tóngshì Pàtèlǐkè láizì Ài'ěrlán.
example.english: My colleague Patrick is from Ireland.
example.fact: Saint Patrick, the patron saint behind the name Patrick, was actually born in Roman Britain, not Ireland — he was kidnapped by Irish raiders as a teenager and only later returned voluntarily as a missionary.

components.note: Hidden — an older semantic root linked to enclosure.
Gives the sound fú, related to rǔ but drifted apart over time.
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了婴儿的乳头周围皮肤。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le yīng'ér de rǔtóu zhōuwéi pífū.
example.english: The doctor examined the skin around the baby's nipple.
example.fact: Male mammals, including humans, retain nipples because the embryo follows the same body plan for both sexes during the first several weeks of development, with sex-specific differences appearing only later through hormonal signals.

components.note: 言 (speech) — 警 relates to speaking out a warning or alarm
敬 (jìng) gives a sound close to 警's reading jǐng, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
糸 (silk thread or cord) — 徽 originally referred to a three-ply cord or sash, the kind worn to mark a rank or office.
微 (wēi) is close in sound to 徽's reading huī, and also carries the sense of something finely wrought or intricate, fitting an emblem's detailed design.

example.hanzi: 那位警察骄傲地展示了他的警徽。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi jǐngchá jiāo'ào de zhǎnshì le tā de jǐnghuī.
example.english: That police officer proudly displayed his badge.
example.fact: The classic five- or six-pointed sheriff's star badge is said to trace back to 19th-century Texas lawmen, who reportedly cut stars out of Mexican peso coins to fashion makeshift badges of authority.

components.note: 口 is a simple picture of an open mouth.
亻 (a person) stands beside the speech component, representing the one doing the speaking.
言 (speech, words) — a person standing firmly by their words gave 信 its meaning 'trustworthy, sincere,' later extended to 'to believe' and 'a letter' (a trusted message).

example.hanzi: 他委托朋友给老板带一个口信。
example.pinyin: Tā wěituō péngyǒu gěi lǎobǎn dài yī gè kǒuxìn.
example.english: He asked a friend to pass on a verbal message to his boss.
example.fact: In West Africa, professional oral historians called griots have for centuries memorized and recited entire family and community histories aloud, preserving genealogies and events across generations without any written records.

components.note: 石 (rock/stone) — 破 relates to breaking, as a rock can be broken
皮 (pí) gives a loose sound connection to 破's reading pò
木 (wood) — 案 originally referred to a wooden table or desk
安 (ān) gives a sound close to 案's reading àn, differing only in tone

example.hanzi: 警方在三天内就破案了。
example.pinyin: Jǐngfāng zài sān tiān nèi jiù pò'àn le.
example.english: The police solved the case within three days.
example.fact: In 1892, Argentine police inspector Juan Vucetich used fingerprint evidence to solve the murder of two children in Necochea, widely considered the first criminal case in history resolved primarily through fingerprint identification.
